land.text: northern Yemen, which Imam Yahya 'declared ... to be independent' on the Ottoman collapse; the infobox lists the Yemen Vilayet as the preceding state

predecessors.note: The Tihamah coast held by Ottoman garrisons until the last force 'surrendered to the British' on 23 January 1919 is left out.

land.text: North Yemen's territory in the unification of 22 May 1990, with the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen

successors.note: Infobox: dissolved 22 May 1990, succeeded by 'Yemen'. The People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (south) merges in the same act; Cliopatria starts its Republic of Yemen row in 1990.

capitals.name: Sanaa
capitals.note: Infobox: Sanaa (1918-1948, 1962-1990); the Mutawakkilite page: 'Its capital was Sanaa from 1918 to 1948, then Taiz from 1948 to 1962.' Imam Yahya was killed on 17 February 1948.

capitals.name: Taiz
capitals.note: Moved under Ahmad bin Yahya in 1948; back to Sanaa after the revolution of 26 September 1962.

rulers.name: Imam Yahya (Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din)
rulers.title: Imam and King
rulers.note: Declared himself ruler of the Zaydi Emirate of Yemen three days after independence (30 October 1918); ambushed and killed on 17 February 1948.

rulers.name: Ahmad bin Yahya
rulers.title: Imam and King
rulers.note: Took control in 1948; 'Imam Ahmad died in September 1962' (no day on the page).

rulers.name: Muhammad al-Badr
rulers.title: Imam and King
rulers.note: Deposed on 26 September 1962 by the coup of Abdullah al-Sallal that created the Yemen Arab Republic.

correction.text: the highlands of northern Yemen under Imam Yahya, without the Tihamah coast still held by Ottoman garrisons

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox has North Yemen 'Established 30 October 1918, independence from the Ottoman Empire', but Cliopatria's row begins in 1919. Imam Yahya 'declared northern Yemen to be independent'; the Mutawakkilite page: the last Ottoman force surrendered to the British on 23 January 1919, so the Tihamah coast is left out of the 1918 shape (168 k km2, 665 cells).

correction.text: the 1919 shape without Al Luhayyah and Hodeidah, which belong to the Idrisid emirate until Yahya captures Hodeidah after 1923

keyframe_review.note: 181.4 k km2 for 1919-1925 against the infobox's 136,000 km2 (ratio 1.33): inside a factor of two, but the shape includes the whole Tihamah, with Al Luhayyah and Hodeidah, which the Asir pages give the Idrisids (Al Luhayyah in 1919, Hodeidah in 1921) and the Mutawakkilite page gives Yahya only 'after 1923', when he 'captured Hudaydah after the death of' al-Idrisi. Corrected for 1919-1923 by cutting the two circles; the ledger returns Hodeidah and Al Luhayyah in 1924. The shape also holds Najran (113 cells), on which the pages opened are silent before 1932, and the rest of the Tihamah (Zabid, Mokha, Midi), which no page gives the Imam before or after 1923 (the British took the surrender of the last Ottoman force on 23 January 1919); those cells stay.

181.3 k km2, the 1919 shape with 2 cells dropped and 1 added, which no page explains. From the ledger's 1924 gain it includes Hodeidah again; the Italo-Yemeni treaty of 1926 recognized Yahya as king of all Yemen. Najran is inside (112 cells), as before; no page opened dates its holders in 1926-1931 (the 1931 skirmish page: a clash of frontier guards at 'Aru 'early in 1931', status quo ante).

151.9 k km2 (ratio 1.12 to the infobox's 136,000): the shape drops Najran and the frontier strip north of 17.4 N (127 cells, bbox 43.3-45.6 E, 17.1-19.1 N). The Saudi-Yemeni war page has the Yemenis advancing on Najran in November 1933 and the Saudis capturing it on 21 April 1934, so Najran was not Yemeni in 1933, which fits a 1932 shape without it; Yemen ceded Najran, Asir and Jizan on 14 June 1934 (Taif). No page opened dates the Saudi occupation of Najran, so the ledger's 1932 loss is a confidence-1 bridge.

151.1 k km2 (ratio 1.11 to the infobox's 136,000 km2): the 1932 shape with 6 cells dropped and 2 added, which no page explains (the Treaty of Taif demarcated the border in 1934, per the war page). The infobox puts the borders as Saudi Arabia to the north, South Yemen to the south and east and the Red Sea to the west. This shape serves the Mutawakkilite kingdom, the 1962 republic and the civil war (the royalist hold on parts of the north has no extent on the pages).

Same polygon as 1936 (151.1 k km2, one cell fewer); it runs to unification on 22 May 1990 ('Official Yemeni unification took place on May 22, 1990'), although Cliopatria ends the row in 1989 and starts its Republic of Yemen in 1990.

region.text: northern Yemen: the highlands around Sanaa

ledger.note: 30 October 1918: Imam Yahya's northern Yemen becomes independent of the Ottoman Empire. Infobox 'Established: 30 October 1918, independence from the Ottoman Empire'; 'Zaydi leader Imam Yahya declared northern Yemen to be independent'; the Mutawakkilite page: three days later he declared himself ruler of the Zaydi Emirate of Yemen. The pages name no frontier.

region.text: the approaches to Aden, to within 50 km of the city

ledger.note: 1922: Imam Yahya attacks Aden. He attacked Aden and advanced to within 50 km, but British air attacks forced a retreat; the page does not say which villages changed hands, so the zone is a radius reading.
1922: the advance on Aden is turned back by British air attacks; in 1934 Yahya 'signed a friendship treaty with the United Kingdom' promising not to attack Aden.

region.text: Hodeidah and Al Luhayyah, the Tihamah coast

ledger.note: Hodeidah returns to Yemen. After 1923 Yahya captured Hudaydah after the death of Idrisi ruler Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi; the page gives no year (the Emirate page dates Muhammad's death 1923, the Province page 1920), so 1924 is the bridge; Al Luhayyah is added because the Saudis took it from Yemen on 1 May 1934 (war page), without a date for its passing from the Idrisids.

region.text: Najran and the frontier strip north of 17.4 N, the cells of the 1919 shape that the 1932 shape drops

ledger.note: Najran and the frontier strip go to the Saudis in Cliopatria's 1932 shape. No page opened dates the Saudi occupation; the war page has the Yemenis advancing on Najran in November 1933 and the Saudis capturing it on 21 April 1934.
November 1933: the Yemenis advance on Najran. 'In November 1933, the Yemenis declared war and advanced on Najran' (a treaty of 1931 was soon broken); the Saudis declared war on 20 March 1934.

region.text: the Yemeni Tihamah and the Hajjah country: Hajara, Luhayya and Hodeidah

ledger.note: May 1934: Saudi forces occupy the Yemeni Tihamah. Saudi Arabia declared war on 20 March 1934; 'Saudi forces captured Hajara and Najran on 7 and 21 April', Luhayya fell on 1 May and Hodeidah on 4 May, and in May the Saudi forces were 'occupying Hodeida'. Ibn Saud's stated aim was to re-occupy townships in the highlands of Tehama. (Reviewer me-10-g: contest_start April changed to occupation_start May to mirror the kingdom-of-saudi-arabia dossier.)

14 June 1934: the Treaty of Taif ends the war. Najran, Asir and Jizan became Saudi; Saudi Arabia withdrew and returned control of Hajjah and Hodeidah to Yemen; Yemen was to pay 100,000 pounds in indemnities.

14 June 1934: Yemen cedes Asir, Najran and Jizan. The Mutawakkilite page: The Taif Treaty was signed and Yemen ceded Asir, Najran and Jizan to Saudi Arabia. The war page's body gives Saudi Arabia 'temporary sovereignty' over them and the infobox says they became Saudi provinces; the treaty demarcated the border. Najran is already outside Cliopatria's shape since 1932.

region.text: the Yemeni Tihamah and the Hajjah country

ledger.note: 7 July 1934: the last Saudi troops leave Yemen after the Treaty of Taif, ending the Saudi occupation of Hajara, Luhayya and Hodeidah.
1948: the capital moves from Sanaa to Taiz. Imam Yahya was ambushed and killed on 17 February 1948; Ahmad bin Yahya took control, and the capital moved to Taiz (infobox: Taiz 1948-1962).

26 September 1962: the Mutawakkilite Kingdom becomes the Yemen Arab Republic. The infobox dates the '26 September Revolution' to 26 September 1962 (the text says 27 September); King Muhammad al-Badr was deposed in the coup led by Abdullah al-Sallal. Same state, same colour.
26 September 1962: the revolution restores Sanaa as the capital (infobox: Sanaa 1962-1990).

region.text: the north and east of Yemen where both armies held ground (Sa'dah, Al Jawf, Ma'rib, Hajjah)

ledger.note: 26 September 1962: the North Yemen Civil War begins between the republic and the royalists of the deposed imam, backed by Saudi Arabia and Jordan; Egypt backed the republic. Late in 1962 a US chargé reported the regime 'in full control of the country, except in some border areas'; the page later has 'Both armies controlled most of the north and east of Yemen, including the towns of Harib and Marib' (undated, after 1965). The governorates are the researcher's reading of 'north and east'.

25 February 1963: Egyptian and republican forces occupy Marib in the Ramadan Offensive; 'On February 25, the forces occupied Marib, and on March 7 they took Harib', and the royalist commander at Harib withdrew to Beihan. The page does not repeat the year; the offensive is dated 1963.

16 July 1965: the royalists retake Marib. 'On July 16, they occupied Marib' (after royalist moves into Sirwah in early June and Qaflan on 14 June). The year is not explicit in the sentence; the page's narrative puts it after 'Between December 1964 and February 1965' and the royalist ambush at Wadi Humaidat on 15 April, so 1965 (reviewer me-10-g corrected 1964 to 1965).

region.text: Sanaa and its airport and the Hodeida road

ledger.note: November 1967: the royalists besiege Sanaa. They surrounded the capital, took its main airport, and cut the highway to Hodeida; the Egyptians then 'relied exclusively on defending a triangle linking Hodeida, Taiz, and San'a'. The page dates the siege November 1967 to February 1968.
February 1968: the siege of Sanaa is lifted. 'By February 1968, the siege was lifted and the republicans had essentially won the war.'

region.text: the north and east of Yemen

ledger.note: 1 December 1970: the civil war ends. The infobox dates it '26 September 1962 - 1 December 1970'; 'In 1970, Saudi Arabia recognized the Republic' and a ceasefire was effected; 'In 1969, sheikhs were brought into the National Assembly'.

region.text: North Yemen, merged with the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen

ledger.note: 22 May 1990: North and South Yemen unite. 'Official Yemeni unification took place on May 22, 1990', after the wars of 1972 and 1979 had put the plans for unification on hold.
22 May 1990: North Yemen ends in the Republic of Yemen. Infobox: dissolved 22 May 1990, succeeded by 'Yemen'.

wars.name: Yemeni attack on Aden
wars.outcome: Yahya's forces reached within 50 km of Aden and were forced back by British air attacks; no border changed.
wars.note: The page also has the Yahya's 1934 friendship treaty with the United Kingdom, promising not to attack Aden.

wars.name: 1931 Saudi-Yemeni border skirmish
wars.outcome: A clash of frontier guards at 'Aru early in 1931; the page's table has 'Military outcome unclear; Status quo ante bellum'.
wars.note: Philby blames the Wahhabi commander for entering Yemeni territory; The Times printed nothing on it in 1931.

wars.name: Saudi-Yemeni war (1934)
wars.outcome: The Saudis took Hajara (7 April), Najran (21 April), Luhayya (1 May) and Hodeidah (4 May 1934); the Treaty of Taif (14 June 1934) gave Asir, Najran and Jizan to Saudi Arabia, returned Hajjah and Hodeidah to Yemen and demarcated the border; the last Saudi troops left on 7 July 1934.
wars.note: The page has the Yemenis advancing on Najran in November 1933 and the Saudis declaring war on 20 March 1934; the Cliopatria shape loses Najran in 1932.

wars.name: North Yemen Civil War

zones.text: the north and east of Yemen (researcher's reading of the page's 'north and east')
the siege of Sanaa, November 1967 to February 1968

wars.outcome: The republicans, helped by Egypt, defeated the royalists, who were backed by Saudi Arabia and Jordan; Egypt recalled 15,000 troops in August 1967, the siege of Sanaa was lifted by February 1968, Saudi Arabia recognized the republic in 1970 and the infobox ends the war on 1 December 1970.
wars.note: Dated places: Sanaa secured 26 September 1962, Egyptian Special Forces at Hodeida 5 October 1962, Marib and Harib taken 25 February and 7 March 1963, Marib retaken by the royalists on 16 July 1965, the siege of Sanaa November 1967 to February 1968; Imam al-Badr survived and went to Saudi Arabia.

wars.name: Yemenite War of 1972
wars.outcome: After the war 'the two states declared that unification would eventually occur'; no border change.

wars.name: Yemenite War of 1979
wars.outcome: The Arab League intervened to stop it; the unification plans 'were put on hold due to the Yemenite War of 1979'; no border change.

certainty.note: Tribal highland frontiers: the Aden Protectorate border and the Najran and Asir frontier are not fixed by any page opened.
The Treaty of Taif (14 June 1934) demarcated the border with Saudi Arabia, so the northern frontier is sharp from 1934; the southern frontier with the Aden Protectorate and South Yemen stays soft.

notes: Five pages opened (North Yemen, Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen, Saudi-Yemeni war (1934), 1931 Saudi-Yemeni border skirmish, North Yemen Civil War) against a budget of up to 5; 'Saudi-Yemeni_War' (without the year) was a disambiguation page and 'Saudi%E2%80%93Yemeni_War' returned url_not_found. One Cliopatria row covers the Mutawakkilite Kingdom (1918-1962) and the Yemen Arab Republic (1962-1990): one state, one colour; the 1962 change is a rename. Cliopatria rows: the 1919-1925 shape carries Al Luhayyah and Hodeidah before Yahya took them (corrected with circles; the Idrisid emirate is the asir dossier), and the 1918 months before the row are added; the 1932 drop of Najran is two years before the Taif cession (a confidence-1 bridge), the 1926 and 1936 changes of a few cells are unexplained. Area: 136,000 km2 against 181.4 k (1919-1931, ratio 1.33), 151.9 k (1932-1935, 1.12) and 151.1 k km2 (1936-1989, 1.11). Not settled: who held Najran 1919-1933; the Aden Protectorate and Dhala frontier (the shape holds Dhala); when Al Luhayyah passed from the Idrisids to Yahya; the exact extent of the royalist-held north in 1962-1970 (the page says only 'most of the north and east'); the page gives no ruler list for the republic (presidents are not in identity.rulers); the 1958 union of Yemen with the United Arab States (March 1958, until the union dissolved after Syria left in September 1961) is an association, not territory (umbrella), and is not drawn; Muhammad al-Badr is dated by 26 September 1962 only. Disagreements: the revolution is 26 September 1962 in the infobox and 27 September in the text; the Saudi-Yemeni war page's infobox says Jizan, Asir and Najran became Saudi provinces while its body gives 'temporary sovereignty'; the war page says the Yemenis advanced on Najran in November 1933; the Mutawakkilite page gives the Taif Treaty on 14 June 1934. Counterparts needing dossiers: yemeni-royalists (the civil war's royalists, 1962-1970, type rebel, extent unknown; group me-10-x), kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd (me-10), asir (this group), people-s-democratic-republic-of-yemen and republic-of-yemen (me-10), united-arab-republic (me-10). The counterpart 'kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd' is used for 1931-1932; the 1933-1934 war events name 'kingdom-of-saudi-arabia' (proclaimed on 23 September 1932 per the Unification of Saudi Arabia page; its dossier starts in September 1932 and holds the mirror events), changed by reviewer me-10-g, who also redated the royalist retaking of Marib to 1965.
